info.name: Store — Checkout & Rewards API
info.description:
Uniblox assessment backend.

Start the app first:
    cd backend && ./mvnw spring-boot:run

**Run Collection works end to end.** Every scenario creates the cart it needs, so no
request depends on another having left the right state behind. Ids and idempotency
keys are captured into collection variables automatically -- nothing to copy by hand.

The only conditional step is the reward coupon: if the next milestone has not been
earned yet, `Admin: generate reward coupon` answers 409 and the three coupon requests
are skipped automatically. Place a few more orders and run again to see them.

Concurrency is the one behaviour this collection cannot show, because Postman sends
requests one at a time. Use the backend test instead:
    ./mvnw test -Dtest=CheckoutConcurrencyTest

Errors carry a stable `code` alongside the RFC 7807 fields, so several distinct 409
conditions stay tellable apart. Branch on `code`, not on the status.

request.description: Liveness plus database connectivity.
Seeded catalogue; prices are integer minor units (cents). Also chooses the best-stocked product for the rest of the run, because checkout genuinely consumes inventory.

exec: // This collection really buys things, so it consumes stock. Pick the best-stocked
// product rather than assuming one, so repeated runs cannot sell it out from under us.
const stocked = products.filter(p => p.inventory >= 10).sort((a, b) => b.inventory - a.inventory);
pm.test('a product has enough stock for this run', () => pm.expect(stocked.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Creates an empty OPEN cart and stores its id in `cartId` for the requests that follow.
The cart as the customer sees it.
Adds a product. Adding does not reserve stock — availability is settled at checkout.
The same product again increments the existing line instead of creating a second row.

exec: pm.test('still a single row for the product', () => pm.expect(lines.length).to.eql(1));

request.description: Replaces the quantity outright — 4 means 4, not 5+4.
Non-positive quantities are rejected by bean validation before any write.
A cart line is capped at 1000 units, which keeps quantity arithmetic away from integer overflow.

This product is not in the cart. Note the code is CART_ITEM_NOT_FOUND, not PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND: update and remove never consult the catalogue, because both cases mean "there is nothing here to change".
A second line, so the removal below does not empty the cart that checkout needs.
Removes the second product and returns the cart with recalculated totals.

exec: pm.test('second product gone', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().items.some(i => i.productId === gone)).to.be.false);

Stock is checked and decremented in one conditional UPDATE, so overselling is impossible. The cart survives.

exec: pm.test('says how much stock there is', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include('in stock'));

request.description: Turns the OPEN cart into an order in one transaction: stock is taken, prices are snapshotted onto the order lines, and the cart becomes CHECKED_OUT.
The order and its snapshot lines: names and prices as captured at checkout, not current catalogue values.
What a client that timed out would send. Returns the original order, creates nothing, touches no inventory.
A new key means a new request, not a retry, so the cart's state refuses it.
A cart that has produced an order is frozen: its contents are the record of what was ordered.
Same guard on update.
Same guard on removal. The cart's contents are unchanged throughout.
Creates a dedicated cart so this scenario does not depend on any other. Saved as `reuseCartId`.
Puts a line in the cart so checkout has something to sell.

request.description: The same key against a different cart is not a retry — it is a different request wearing the same name.
Creates a dedicated cart so this scenario does not depend on any other. Saved as `emptyCartId`.
An empty cart cannot be checked out.
The header is mandatory. A blank value is rejected the same way.
Issues the coupon for the next unrewarded milestone, if enough successful orders have been placed. If the milestone is not yet reached this answers 409 and the coupon requests below are skipped.

exec: pm.test('201 issued, or 409 not yet earned', () => pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));
// Skip the coupon requests. Feature-detected so it works on old and new Postman.
